messages:
alex: heads up — after the fp16 kernel fallback rolled to canary we've seen a big warmup hit-rate drop on several low-cardinality routes. 92% -> ~58% for v2/chat-longcontext around 11:02. :confused:
sophia: ouch. which rollout ID / build? can you paste the short numbers and a couple metrics? :eyes:
alex: rollout id 2026-03-17-canary-7, build 2026031701. Samples from the morning: prefix_cache.hits=582 prefix_cache.requests=1000 hit_rate=58.2% (previously ~920/1000). p50 latency unchanged but p95 up ~30ms.
kevin: any model change too or just runtime kernel swap + quant profile?
alex: no model version change — same open-llama-13b:v3. We switched kernel variant for attention to use fused-attn-fallback.fp16 on canary. Quant flags same (q4_0 runtime).
ci-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout 2026-03-17 11:02 finished for runtime-group-a (10% traffic). Logs and artifacts: https://ci.example/rollouts/20260317-canary-7
sophia: can you dump a couple prefix keys (hashed) for hits vs misses? want to confirm keying mismatch vs cache eviction/warmup pattern.
alex: quick sample (anonymized):
```
# hits
k=md5("user:app:v2:/conv/seed=239" ) -> 0x7a1f2b
k=md5("user:app:v2:/conv/seed=240" ) -> 0x3c9b12
# misses
k=md5("user:app:v2:/conv/seed=239 " ) -> 0x8f11aa  # note trailing space
k=md5("user:app:v2:/conv/seed=241") -> 0x3c9b12
```
kevin: whoa trailing space in a key there — that smells like tokenizer normalization or a different canonicalization pipeline. Did the fused-attn change also touch input preprocessing?
alex: we checked codepaths: no deliberate tokenizer changes. But the fallback fused-attn kernel uses a slightly different padding routine to reorder tensors — it's possible we ended up using a different tokenization-normalization branch in the runtime shim for speed.
lisa: could also be subtle whitespace normalization differences from the compiler/serializer used for kernel inputs. We've seen identical-looking upstream strings produce different canonical keys when the serialization layout changed.
sophia: ok reproduce steps please so infra can verify determinism: 1) curl sample request to canary endpoint with seed=239 2) inspect prefix key exposed on request context (enable DEBUG_PREFIX_KEY) 3) compare to pre-rollout artifacts.
alex: repro script (quick):
```
curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.internal/v2/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b:v3","input":"<conv seed=239>hello","debug":"prefix_key"}'
```
kevin: while you repro, please also run the small profiler snippet to capture KV lookup time:
```
perfdump --addr $PID --metric kv_lookup,kv_miss_latency --out /tmp/kvp.json
jq . /tmp/kvp.json | grep kv_miss_latency
```
alex: attached profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
kv_lookup_count: 1000
kv_hit_count: 582
kv_miss_count: 418
kv_miss_latency_p95_ms: 18.2   # before: ~7.4
kv_lookup_cpu_us_per_op: 320  # before: 120
```
sophia: miss_latency up +10ms p95 — consistent with extra work on key comparisons / normalization. That matches canonicalization mismatch hypothesis. If keys differ because of trailing whitespace or different token join order, we get misses then heavier KV processing.
lisa: quick mitigations: 1) enable key-normalization shim to strip trailing spaces before hashing (cheap, safe) 2) short-term: route affected customers to older kernel via smart-routing 3) long-term: make serializer stable test in runtime CI.
kevin: +1 for key-normalization shim as immediate hotfix. Any downsides? Could mask real upstream differences but we only normalize whitespace and unify token join.
alex: implemented a small patch locally that trims and canonicalizes token join order. Quick A/B on canary (10 requests) shows hit_rate -> 90% for sample seeds. I'll push canary patch to hotfix branch now.
sophia: nice. after patch please run a wider sweep (1000 requests across multiple seeds) and check prefix collision risk (i.e., over-normalization merging two distinct prefixes).
alex: agreed — I'll run the sweep. plan: rollback fallback kernel if normalization patch fails, otherwise ship shim to prod and add CI test.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: hotfix-branch created: runtime/hotfix/prefix-normalize-3345678910, queued for canary deploy.
lisa: also add a test in perf CI that diffs prefix-key output between kernel variants for 50 random inputs — fail if >0.1% new-key divergence.
kevin: and add a telemetry metric: prefix_key_variants_count per request to track how many distinct canonical keys we saw for same user+seed within 1h window.
sophia: good. Alex, let us know sweep numbers and whether p95 KV latency returns to baseline. :thumbsup:
alex: will do. starting sweep now — posting results in this thread in ~15m.
ci-bot: perf-alert: canary p95 KV latency exceeded threshold for runtime-group-a at 11:05, auto-notification sent to #eng-oncall.
alex: ack, stepping off to triage. thanks all.
